title: Integral proper base change on localizing categories
statement:
For a cartesian square with $p:X\to Y$ proper, $g:Y'\to Y$, $p':X'\to Y'$ and
$g':X'\to X$, the base change map $g^*Rp_*\to Rp'_*g'^*$ is an isomorphism of
functors $\Loc(\Dbc(X,\mathcal O_E))\to\Loc(\Dbc(Y',\mathcal O_E))$.

proof.text: Use the standing scheme and coefficient setting [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]: the four schemes are separated of finite type over a field of positive characteristic different from $\ell$, the arrows are morphisms over that field, and $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ is finite with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$. For $K\in\Dbc(X,\mathcal O_E)$, clause (3) of [det-thm-sfb-proper-base-change-integral] states that the canonical ordinary proper base-change map $\beta_K:g^*Rp_*K\to Rp'_*g'^*K$ is an isomorphism. Its clause (1) places $Rp_*K$ in $\Dbc(Y,\mathcal O_E)$; [sk-lem-integral-models] (3) preserves $\Dbc$ under $g^*$ and $g'^*$, and [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence] (b) gives properness of $p'$, so the same clause (1) for $p'$ places the other endpoint in $\Dbc(Y',\mathcal O_E)$. Thus the transformation to be extended is already invertible on the bounded constructible generators, with the ordinary module-object coefficients and ordinary inverse images used in the statement.

source.place: Proof paragraph, first sentence (invertibility on Dbc), using the existing stronger integral theorem; its blueprint proof, clause (3), supplies the finite-reduction and derived-completeness argument.

proof.text: The functors $g^*Rp_*$ and $Rp'_*g'^*$ restrict to exact functors between the indicated localizing categories and preserve all small direct sums. Indeed [det-proper-image-localizing-proper] gives these properties for proper direct images with $\mathcal O_E$ coefficients, while [det-proper-base-change-unbounded-pullback] gives them for both inverse images; [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence] supplies properness of $p'$. The opening assertion of [sk-lem-integral-models] gives $\Dctf(T,\mathcal O_E)=\Dbc(T,\mathcal O_E)$ for each of the four standing schemes $T$. Their localizing closures are therefore equal: in the definition [sk-def-localizing-closure] the collections of full replete triangulated subcategories containing the generators and closed under ambient sums are identical. Hence both composites have exactly the source and target in the statement. For every edge $u$, clause (1) and the final paragraph of [sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients] identify $u^{-1}\mathcal O_{E,T}$ with $\mathcal O_{E,T'}$ and make module pullback exact. The coefficient identifications come from pullback of the same condensed ring along the structure maps to the point, so the two composites around the square agree. The exact-functor clause of [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories] identifies $Lu^*$ canonically with the termwise functor $D(u^*)$. Under these identifications, [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition] states that the derived pullback composition comparison $c_{h,k}$ is, on a K-flat complex with flat terms, the class of the termwise canonical isomorphism of module pullbacks; its coefficient-compatibility hypothesis is the agreement of the two composite identifications just checked. On each term this sheaf-level isomorphism is the one of [def-sfb-module-upper-star-comp]: both are natural isomorphisms $(kh)^*\cong h^*k^*$ between left adjoints whose conjugate [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate] is the composition isomorphism $k_*h_*\cong(kh)_*$ of direct images, which on underlying sheaves is the identity of sections $G(Z\times_W(W\times_VT))=G(Z\times_VT)$ in both constructions; conjugation is a bijection, so the two pullback comparisons coincide. Since $u^*$ is exact, every complex computes $Lu^*$ termwise, so the composite $\theta$ of step 3 and the $\theta_\square$ of [def-weil-pbc-ambient-ringed-exchange] agree; the derived adjunctions give the corresponding units and counits. Thus [def-weil-pbc-ambient-ringed-exchange] gives precisely the unit/comparison/counit transformation of the extension lemma in step 3. Its component is $\beta_K=Rp'_*g'^*(\varepsilon_{p,K})\circ Rp'_*(\theta_{Rp_*K})\circ\eta_{p',g^*Rp_*K}$, where $\theta:p'^*g^*\cong g'^*p^*$. All operations and sums are in the ordinary unbounded module-object categories specified by [sk-def-localizing-closure].

source.place: Proof paragraph, second sentence: exactness and direct-sum preservation on the localizing categories

proof.text: Apply [det-proper-base-change-unbounded-extension] with $\Lambda=\mathcal O_E$ and the given cartesian square. Its scheme setting and admissible coefficient hypotheses are those fixed in step 1. It specifies the very same base-change map as step 2: the unit for $p'$, the canonical comparison of the two composed pullbacks, and the counit for $p$, in that order. In particular its conclusion concerns the stated canonical morphism. By the opening assertion of [sk-lem-integral-models], $\Dctf(X,\mathcal O_E)=\Dbc(X,\mathcal O_E)$, so step 1 proves invertibility on every generator required in that lemma's hypothesis. Its conclusion gives invertibility on $\Loc(\Dctf(X,\mathcal O_E))=\Loc(\Dbc(X,\mathcal O_E))$. Together with the restricted functor types from step 2, this proves the claimed isomorphism of functors. The extension lemma states the result for this specified exchange transformation; no inference from mere naturality to shift compatibility is needed.

source.place: Final two sentences: extension by localizing determination, using the existing generic extension lemma in the explicitly cited proper-base-change-unbounded unit.

Step 2: det-proper-image-localizing-proper (its unconditional O_E paragraph) and the pullback node give exact sum-preserving functors on Loc; Dctf=Dbc gives Loc(Dctf)=Loc(Dbc). Step 3: the extension lemma's hypotheses hold (O_E admissible, square cartesian, p proper) and its beta_K is the item's map, so step 1 discharges its Dctf hypothesis and it gives invertibility on all of Loc.
